subject: Clarify pen-test scope + SOC2 evidence for MSA / Order Form
messages:
From: Elliot Barnes <elliot.barnes@helixhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Megan Walsh <megan.walsh@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on pen-test access & SOC 2 evidence for MSA/Order Form

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form — we're getting close on commercial terms. Before procurement can greenlight the PO, InfoSec has a few open items in the security exhibit/redlines attached: Helix_MSA_redlines.pdf (see p.2-4). Quick summary of the asks from our side:

- Confirm you'll provide a current SOC 2 Type II report and whether Redwood will provide complementary bridge letters for the covered period.
- Clarify pen-test language: we want (a) confirmation of an annual external pen test covering production tenant isolation, (b) an option for an on-site or vendor-led review if we move forward with a Redwood Private deployment, and (c) allowed tester requirements (accreditation).
- Evidence cadence: procurement wants an explicit timeline of when evidence (SOC2 + pen-test report + remediation plan) will be provided during contract execution — procurement needs these on file before signing.

We attached our marked-up MSA; the key redlines are the audit-rights paragraph and the definition of "Provider Systems". Can we get confirmation on whether the hosted environment entitles us to production-level access, or if we will receive scoped artifacts (logs, KV cache metrics, deployment manifests) instead?

Proposed dates: if a pen-test is required pre-commit, we prefer a window in early January 2027 (2027-01-10 to 2027-01-21). If Redwood can provide the SOC2 + pen-test report from your latest run, procurement may sign earlier and schedule a focused verification after go-live.

Can we hop on a short call tomorrow to align?

Thanks,
Elliot Barnes
Security Lead | Helix Health

Subject: Re: Questions on pen-test access & SOC 2 evidence for MSA/Order Form

Elliot — thanks for the clear summary and the marked MSA. I pulled the team in (cc'd Karthik from Legal and Monica from CS). High level responses below and we can detail on a quick call:

- SOC 2: attached is our most recent SOC 2 Type II attestation (Redwood_SOC2-report-2025.pdf). We provide the full report and a short bridge memo for the covered period.
- Pen test: Redwood conducts an annual external penetration test; we can share the executive summary and remediation confirmation. For Private (on-prem/VPC) deployments we can accommodate a customer-contracted tester with scoping controls (see proposed process below).
- Evidence access: For Hosted customers we do not grant direct host-level access; we deliver scoped artifacts (audit logs, access logs, config manifests, and a penetration-test executive report). For Private, we can provide a bastion/jumpbox or host-level access under a scoped NDA and supervised session.

Proposed process (mutual action plan):
1) Agree scope in writing (target systems, date range, excluded IPs).
2) Sign an NDA + pen-test SOW (attached: PenTest-SOW-v1.docx).
3) For Hosted: Redwood provides artifacts and remediation statements within 10 business days after report delivery.
4) For Private: coordinate on-site or remote vendor access; production access limited to agreed windows and monitored sessions.

Karthik — can you confirm acceptable contract language around "audit rights" and specify any hard limits on frequency or scope we should push back on?

Elliot — I can do a 30 min call tomorrow (Wed) at 10:30am PT to walk through — does that work?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pen-test access & SOC 2 evidence for MSA/Order Form

Thanks Aditya — the report and SOW are helpful. A few clarifications from InfoSec after review:

- Frequency: we expect up to two pen-tests per 12-month contract term if there is a major change flagged by Helix (e.g., processing of a new regulated dataset). Is Redwood open to "one annual standard test plus one conditional test triggered by change" language?
- Tester accreditation: we prefer testers with CREST or OSCP-equivalent certification and a documented chain of custody for any artifacts pulled during testing.
- On-site access: if we sign for a Private deployment, we still need to ensure the order form includes a clause that allows our approved vendor to perform remote authenticated testing with a red-team account for up to 3 business days in the agreed window.
- Audit-rights redline: see page 3 of our redlines — we specifically removed language that would require full control-plane access. We are OK with scoped access if there is a clear articulation of what "scoped" means (examples are good).

Proposed pen-test window remains 2027-01-10 to 2027-01-21. If Redwood can commit to the SOC2 + pen-test executive summary now and accept the conditional second test approach, procurement should be able to progress on the PO.

One more ask: can you add a sentence to the MSA or order form that requires Redwood to notify Helix of high-severity findings within 72 hours of discovery? That will satisfy internal risk owners.

Best,
Elliot

Attachment: Helix_MSA_redlines.pdf (updated)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Elliot Barnes <elliot.barnes@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pen-test access & SOC 2 evidence for MSA/Order Form

Team / Elliot — legal has reviewed Helix's marked redlines. We can accept most of the asks with the following commercial/legal guardrails:

1) Frequency: "One annual independent penetration test per contract year, plus one conditional test where reasonably necessary and agreed upon in writing (triggered by material change)." We will not agree to unlimited or undefined audit frequency.

2) Scope & Access: For Hosted deployments, Redwood will provide an executive pen-test report, remediation statements, and scoped artifact sets (audit logs, access logs, configuration snapshots) — we will not permit unescorted host-level access for hosted tenants. For Private deployments, subject to an executed NDA and SOW, we will permit remote authenticated testing through a temporary role and supervised bastion/jumpbox access for a limited window (we propose max 3 business days).

3) Tester requirements: we can accept a requirement for testers with recognized qualifications (e.g., CREST or equivalent). We will require advance notice of the vendor and proof of insurance.

4) Notification of high severity: Redwood accepts a 72-hour notification SLA for confirmed high-severity findings that materially affect Helix data. Notification will include impact summary and initial mitigation plan; full remediation timelines to follow.

5) Contract language: below is a concise clause we propose for inclusion in the security exhibit (suggest this as redline to page 3):

"Provider conducts an annual independent penetration test and will provide Customer an executive summary and remediation confirmation within 10 business days of receiving the final report. Customer may request one additional conditional penetration test per contract year upon demonstration of a material change; such request will be subject to a mutually agreed SOW and an executed NDA. For Hosted services, Provider will not permit direct host-level access; Provider will deliver scoped artifacts as reasonably requested. For Private deployments, Provider will permit remote authenticated testing in a supervised environment for a maximum of three (3) business days during an agreed testing window. Provider will notify Customer of confirmed high-severity findings within seventy-two (72) hours of verification and will provide an initial mitigation plan."

If that language looks acceptable, Aditya, please propose it back to Helix and confirm the proposed pen-test window and the HubSpot deal (deal HXL-2026-089) so Commercial can tee up the order form signature. Monica, please prepare a short runbook for handing off artifacts and a sample evidence package.

-Karthik

Subject: Re: Questions on pen-test access & SOC 2 evidence for MSA/Order Form — proposed next steps

Elliot — appreciate the fast turnaround. Summarizing agreed items and next steps so procurement has a single doc to action:

Agreed points:
- Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report and bridge memo today (delivered earlier in thread).
- Pen-test cadence: one annual test + one conditional test per contract year (as defined by Karthik's clause).
- Hosted customers: no host-level access; we will deliver scoped artifacts and the pen-test executive summary.
- Private customers: remote authenticated testing allowed under NDA + SOW, supervised via bastion for up to 3 business days.
- Notification SLA: Redwood will notify Helix of confirmed high-severity findings within 72 hours and share an initial mitigation plan.

Immediate asks for Helix procurement to finish the PO:
1) Confirm acceptance of the clause Karthik proposed (pasted in his email).
2) Confirm pen-test window: we can tentatively reserve 2027-01-10 to 2027-01-21 for the primary test cycle — please confirm if that works for your vendor.
3) Approve the attached PenTest-SOW-v1.docx and we will sign an NDA/DocuSign order form. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/helloworld/doc/HXL-089-orderform

I'll get Monica to send the evidence runbook and a sample artifact bundle to your security mailbox as well. If you confirm acceptance and dates, Commercial will issue the final order form for signature and Procurement can progress the PO.

Thanks and speak soon,
